# Annotated manifesto pilot: selection and evidence audit

## Selection

Strategy, §§180–206, was selected as the strongest verified cluster in the six reception texts inspected for this pilot. This is a bounded qualitative selection, not a census of the entire dissertation archive. The Power Process and the opening discussion of leftism were alternative candidates; Strategy supplied the clearest concentration of explicit paragraph references across all six checked readers. Section length differs, so raw counts cannot establish normalized reception density.

A keyword triage of 196 attached newspaper pages found zero page-URL hits for “power process” or “surrogate activit…”, four for “leftism/oversocialization”, and 30 for revolution/strategy terms. These are OCR search hits, not verified engagements, and were excluded from annotation counts and the selection claim.

The strongest initial reading route is §§183, 188, 189, 200, 206. The section is reproduced continuously, including paragraphs with no verified annotation. Absence of a marker means not yet annotated, not no historical reception.

## Base text

The reading text is the Anarchist Library transcription, whose source note identifies Technological Slavery, not a facsimile of the September 1995 newspaper supplement. Its numbered paragraphs are preserved. Edition differences, OCR/typographic errors, and early printings have not been exhaustively collated. Wikimedia Commons describes the manifesto as author-dedicated public domain: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Industrial_Society_and_Its_Future.pdf .

## Counting

A response record may cover multiple paragraphs. A paragraph badge counts distinct sources, not repeated quotations or rehostings. The graph shows paragraph/source incidence, not influence, agreement, or organizational membership. Hosted dates are not silently treated as composition dates.

## Annotation records

### sale-nature — §§183, 184

Kirkpatrick Sale, Unabomber’s Secret Treatise: Is There Method in His Madness?. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/kirkpatrick-sale-unabomber-s-secret-treatise

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraph beginning “In short, it feels to me…”.

Sale reads the appeal to nature as instrumental rather than an expression of ecological understanding. He questions what the symbol does for the proposed ideology.

### sale-core — §§187, 188, 189

Kirkpatrick Sale, Unabomber’s Secret Treatise: Is There Method in His Madness?. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/kirkpatrick-sale-unabomber-s-secret-treatise

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraph beginning “But it doesn’t much matter to him…”.

Sale brings the differentiated audiences together and compares the proposed political relationship to Leninism.

### sale-revolution — §§193

Kirkpatrick Sale, Unabomber’s Secret Treatise: Is There Method in His Madness?. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/kirkpatrick-sale-unabomber-s-secret-treatise

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraphs beginning “He says that…” and “This is a somewhat peculiar position…”.

Sale juxtaposes the possibility of a non-armed revolution with the author’s actual bombings and destructive rhetoric. He finds the relation between means and ends unresolved.

### luke-unknown — §§180

Timothy W. Luke, Re-Reading the Unabomber Manifesto. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/tim-luke-re-reading-the-unabomber-manifesto

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraph beginning “In many ways, the Unabomber only seems committed…”.

Luke turns the charge of recklessness back on the proposed revolution: what would prevent its leaders from reproducing the uncertainty they condemn?

### luke-destruction — §§182

Timothy W. Luke, Re-Reading the Unabomber Manifesto. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/tim-luke-re-reading-the-unabomber-manifesto

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraph ending with the citation “(¶182)”.

Luke reads the refusal to design a successor society alongside the commitment to revolutionary leadership. Destruction does not resolve the problem of who would exercise power.

### luke-core — §§189

Timothy W. Luke, Re-Reading the Unabomber Manifesto. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/tim-luke-re-reading-the-unabomber-manifesto

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Paragraph beginning “The revolutionaries of the Unabomber’s Freedom Club…”.

Luke interprets the committed minority as a political vanguard. His criticism concerns the organization of authority, not simply the stated opposition to technology.

### luke-justice — §§200, 201

Timothy W. Luke, Re-Reading the Unabomber Manifesto. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/tim-luke-re-reading-the-unabomber-manifesto

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Discussion of social justice as a revolutionary goal, ending with the citation (¶201).

Luke connects the exclusion of social justice to the demand to eliminate organization-dependent technology. He questions the social arrangements implied by that priority.

### fulano-goal — §§206

T. Fulano / David Watson, The Unabomber and the Future of Industrial Society. https://www.fifthestate.org/archive/348-fall-1996/the-unabomber-and-the-future-of-industrial-society/

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Concluding paragraph beginning “Connected to people and place…”.

Fulano directly contests the single-goal formulation. He presents commitments to people, place, and mutual aid as irreducible to technological destruction.

### faun-nature — §§183, 184

Formerly Feral Faun, Fixed Ideas and Letter Bombs. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/wolfi-landstreicher-fixed-ideas-and-letter-bombs

Relationship: Discussion. Locator: Section “FC’s Fixed Idea #2”; paragraph beginning “Those who have a cause…”.

Feral Faun objects to the proposed opposition between wild nature and industrial technology as a manipulative ideology. The objection concerns its compatibility with autonomy.

### faun-audience — §§187, 188

Formerly Feral Faun, Fixed Ideas and Letter Bombs. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/wolfi-landstreicher-fixed-ideas-and-letter-bombs

Relationship: Discussion. Locator: Section “FC’s Fixed Idea #2”; discussion of propagandising and group dynamics.

Feral Faun reads the propaganda strategy as producing a group in which a few lead and most follow. This is a conceptual connection to these paragraphs; no paragraph number is supplied in that passage.

### faun-goal — §§200, 206

Formerly Feral Faun, Fixed Ideas and Letter Bombs. https://www.thetedkarchive.com/library/wolfi-landstreicher-fixed-ideas-and-letter-bombs

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: Section “FC’s Fixed Idea #2”; passage quoting the ONLY goal and no competing goal.

Feral Faun quotes the overriding-goal language and objects to subordinating individual life to a cause. Self-determination is the standard against which the proposed strategy is judged.

### moore-nature — §§183

John Moore, Beyond the Fragments: A Reaction to Industrial Society and Its Future. https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/john-moore-beyond-the-fragments-a-reaction-to-industrial-society-and-its-future

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: “Ideology and strategy”; quotation introduced as Thesis 183.

Moore quotes §183 and argues that the opposition between nature and culture remains an ideological construction. Invoking wildness does not, in his reading, escape civilization’s categories.

### moore-audience — §§187, 188

John Moore, Beyond the Fragments: A Reaction to Industrial Society and Its Future. https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/john-moore-beyond-the-fragments-a-reaction-to-industrial-society-and-its-future

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: “Ideology and strategy”; quotation introduced as Theses 187, 188.

Moore quotes §§187–188 together. He reads the distinction between sophisticated readers and an unthinking majority as reproducing hierarchy and class power.

### moore-goal — §§200, 201, 206

John Moore, Beyond the Fragments: A Reaction to Industrial Society and Its Future. https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/john-moore-beyond-the-fragments-a-reaction-to-industrial-society-and-its-future

Relationship: Quotation. Locator: “Ideology and strategy”; composite quotation introduced as Theses 200, 201, 206.

Moore joins §§200, 201, and 206 in a composite quotation. He challenges the primacy of a single goal and the political authority implied by excluding other commitments.

### ur-destruction — §§182

Último Reducto, Comments on the communiques from Individualists Tending toward the Wild. https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/ultimo-reducto-comments-on-the-communiques-from-individualists-tending-toward-the-wild

Relationship: Explicit citation. Locator: Numbered point 4; paragraph explicitly citing 104 and 182.

UR cites §182, alongside §104, to dispute the claim that revolution necessarily entails designing a new society. The annotation records UR’s rebuttal, not an independent verification of ITS’s position.

### ur-majority — §§189

Último Reducto, Comments on the communiques from Individualists Tending toward the Wild. https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/ultimo-reducto-comments-on-the-communiques-from-individualists-tending-toward-the-wild

Relationship: Explicit citation. Locator: Numbered point 4; paragraph explicitly citing 189.

UR cites §189 against the position attributed to ITS that Kaczynski advocates educating the majority into opposition. The same paragraph criticized as vanguardist becomes evidence in a dispute over fidelity.
